title.narrative: BT Strengthening of the Public Procurement Policy Division

description.narrative: The RGoB recently established a Public Procurement Policy Division (PPPD), under the Departnment of National Properties of the Ministry of Finance, to handle all matters related to public procurement in Bhutan. This division has only been in existance since August 2008 and has just three full time staff; none of which are procurement experts. The PPPD, therefore, needs a lot of assistance to allow it to become operational and successful in the long run. An IDF is perfectly placed as a financial instrument to assist with such a situation whereby the institution first needs to be built up (i.e. operationalize) and then start implementing reforms and fullfiling their mandates. This IDF will aim to assist the PPPD in areas of institutional reforms, regulatory reforms, capacity building, access to information and public awareness, and setting up the the foundations for monitoring and electronic procurement systems. This will need to be done with the assistance of various consultants who have the necessary expertise. These consultants will be made to part their knowledge on the PPPD staff as they fullfil their TOR, so that after their departure the capacity of the division to do such jobs are retained. Eventhough various consultants will be needed to carry out the IDF's activities, the idea is that the staff of the PPPD are involved actively and actually learn how to do it themselves. Since only three full time staff are available at the PPPD at this stage, the IDF needs to envisage some longer term national consultants to assist with manpower for the initial years of the division's existance. Some of the activities under the grant include; the creation of an operations manual and job descriptions for the PPPD staff, the creation of short, medium and long term procurement reform strategies, conducting an OECD/DAC Procurement Self Assessment, establishing a reporting and monitoring strategy for procurement, setting up an electronic platform for electronic procurement systems in Bhutan, creating a complaints mechanism, creating specific procurement documents related to procurement of ICT equipment or health products, building the capacity of the PPPD staff through on the job training, training from consultants, specialized skills training and study tours, and drafting and implementing a communications strategy. The development objective of this IDF proposal is to put in place the foundations for the creation of a professional and efficient center of excellence within government that can manage the public procurement function in Bhutan on a sustainable basis.
